boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten named Arboretum stops for a no-purchase outdoor meet-up, using the College’s public free-tour and collection-access policy.

cards.title: Walk the Nature Trail
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Meet at the trailhead and walk a section together; keep bikes off the trail and coordinate with the Arboretum before bringing a planned large group.
cards.short_summary: A 2.2-mile campus-perimeter walk with woods, meadows, and pond views.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s Living Collections Policy says the Arboretum provides open and reasonable access and offers free campus tours to the public; the Nature Trail is a named Arboretum route.
cards.access_notes: Use the trail as a self-guided visit; large planned groups must contact the Arboretum first. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Watch for Wildlife at Duck Pond
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Bring a friend, pause at the pond edge, and look quietly for birds, fish, turtles, and frogs without feeding or disturbing wildlife.
cards.short_summary: A three-acre campus pond and a natural observation stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Duck Pond is a named Haverford Arboretum highlight; the College’s Living Collections Policy provides open and reasonable access and states that free campus tours are regularly offered to the public.
cards.access_notes: Stay on appropriate paths and do not feed waterfowl. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Meet Beneath the Treaty Elm
cards.subtitle: Barclay Beach, Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Use the lawn by Barclay Hall as a conversation stop, then read the Arboretum history for the remaining elm from the 1915 planting.
cards.short_summary: A named historic elm on the Barclay Beach lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford identifies the Treaty Elm as the remaining tree from seven American elm grafts planted behind Barclay Hall; its Arboretum policy provides open access and free public campus tours.
cards.access_notes: Visit as part of an outdoor Arboretum walk; do not climb trees. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Read Tree Labels in the Ryan Pinetum
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Walk together through the conifer collection and compare the labels; the Pinetum’s tree labels include botanical names and family names.
cards.short_summary: An 18-acre conifer collection for a slow, label-led walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford identifies the Ryan Pinetum as a named Arboretum collection and documents its tree-label system; the policy provides open access and free public campus tours.
cards.source_title: State Champion Trees | Arboretum | Haverford College
cards.access_notes: Remain on appropriate paths and leave plant material in place. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Look for the Asian Gardens’ Artifacts
cards.subtitle: Beside the Dining Center, Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Take a short outdoor loop beside the Dining Center and identify the garden features together; enjoy the setting without entering dining facilities.
cards.short_summary: Two named gardens with landscape design and donated artifacts.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford identifies the Gertrude C. Teaf Garden and Denis Asian Garden as its Asian Gardens; the Arboretum policy provides open access and free public campus tours.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor garden visit beside the Dining Center. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Visit Haverfarm’s Outdoor Growing Area
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Meet by the farm signage and discuss what is growing; observe the educational farm space without harvesting produce or entering work areas.
cards.short_summary: A named year-round farm and educational space on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford describes Haverfarm as a year-round farming and educational space for students, faculty, staff, and community members; the Arboretum policy provides open access and free public campus tours.
cards.source_title: Sustainable Haverford | Haverford College Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Observe from public outdoor areas and do not harvest. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.entity_name: Penn State Certified Pollinator Garden Walk
cards.title: Trace the Pollinator Garden
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to Duck Pond, Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Walk the garden edge with friends and look for insects and flowering plants; keep clear of planted areas and leave all plants and wildlife undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A named 10-acre certified pollinator garden beside Duck Pond.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s campus map identifies a Penn State Certified Pollinator Garden adjacent to Duck Pond; the Arboretum policy provides open access and free public campus tours.
cards.source_title: Sustainable Haverford | Haverford College Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Stay on paths around planted areas. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Inspect the VCAM Rain Garden
cards.subtitle: Visual Culture, Arts, and Media building, Haverford College
cards.notes: Meet outside VCAM and follow the rain garden’s planted edge, comparing how its landscaping relates to the building’s runoff-management purpose.
cards.short_summary: A named rain garden outside the VCAM building.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s campus map identifies a rain garden outside the Visual Culture, Arts, and Media building; the Arboretum policy provides open access and free public campus tours.
cards.source_title: Sustainable Haverford | Haverford College Campus Map
cards.access_notes: View from public outdoor areas and avoid planted beds. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Pause at the Peace Garden
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Make this a quiet outdoor conversation stop, then continue the campus walk; respect the garden beds and leave any plants, flowers, and seeds in place.
cards.short_summary: A named additional area of interest within Haverford’s Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford lists the Peace Garden as an Arboretum area of interest; the College’s Living Collections Policy provides open and reasonable collection access and states that free campus tours are regularly offered to the public.
cards.access_notes: Use as an outdoor Arboretum stop; do not walk in flower beds or harvest plants. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Take a Hilles Garden Loop
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Add the garden to a short campus loop and compare seasonal planting as you walk; keep to accessible paths and treat the beds as display areas.
cards.short_summary: A named additional garden area within the Haverford Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford lists Hilles Garden as an Arboretum area of interest; the College’s Living Collections Policy provides open and reasonable collection access and states that free campus tours are regularly offered to the public.
cards.access_notes: Use public outdoor paths and do not enter flower beds. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.
